newsitem.title: USA: G.E. Medical appointment pleases analysts.
newsitem.headline: G.E. Medical appointment pleases analysts.

text.p: The appointment of Jeffrey Immelt as president and chief executive of G.E. Medical Systems, a unit of General Electric Co, was welcomed by industry analysts on Thursday.

"Immelt is very innovative, dynamic, and he's kind of a visionary type guy who sees the trends and where they will lead the business in four or five years," said Nicholas Heymann, an analyst at Natwest Securities Corp.
Earlier, GE said that Immelt, 40, would replace John Trani, who left to become chairman and chief executive of The Stanley Works, a hardware maker based in New Britain, Conn.
Immelt was formerly vice president of the Americas at GE Plastics, where was successful in improving performance of that unit, analysts said.
"Immelt had a good track record at GE Plastics and was able to improve returns in a difficult (industry) environment," said Bill Fiala, an analyst at Edward D. Jones in St. Louis.
"The $4 billion Medical Systems is a very significant, prominent business within GE," Heymann said.
He said the Milwaukee-based unit was showing top-line growth in the mid-single digits, compared with an industry average of one to two percent.

"Immelt's biggest challenge is to continue to expand the service and after-market business in the more mature markets of Europe and the U.S.," Heymann said. "Hardware per se is not going to be the growth business it was in the '80s."
Under Trani, G.E. Medical became the dominant player in the ultrasound business, and also expanded its service business, said Heymann.
Trani, 51, worked at Fairfield, Conn.-based G.E. since 1978. He was president and chief executive of G.E. Medical since 1986. ((Hartford newsroom (860) 727-0224))
